title: The Last Crossing

voice.name: Liam
voice.direction: Intimate, controlled storyteller; build curiosity without shouting; dry centered delivery; native pitch and tempo. Quoted character intent is performed by the same narrator; no extra voice.

hook: Lucia bought the last crossing, then watched the ferryman sell the same two seats to somebody else.
alternative_hooks: The last ferry had left. So who was selling them tickets?
Lucia paid for an exit that did not exist.
alternative_hook_use: Replace scene 1 and re-time/recount the master before production; do not append.
script: Lucia bought the last crossing, then watched the ferryman sell the same two seats to somebody else. The other passengers carried luggage. Jason carried an envelope that suddenly felt much too heavy for paper. Lucia checked the timetable. The last boat had left before they arrived. This one was staying tied. Across the creek, headlights appeared between trees. Their anonymous buyer had chosen a meeting with no exit. Jason reached for the money. Lucia reached for the waiting family's bags and carried them back uphill. The buyer flashed his lights, impatient. Jason finally understood: witnesses were supposed to leave on that boat. Lucia handed their fare to the family. Everyone waited together beneath the shelter until the headlights vanished. At sunrise, the real ferry arrived. They crossed without the deal. Jason called the lost money cheap.
plot_mechanism: incomplete transport schedule exposes a witness-isolation trap
